title: Compare and order decimals to hundredths

lesson.title: Which Decimal Is Bigger?

steps.say: You already know how to read decimals like zero point two five, and you know which digit is the tenths and which is the hundredths. Today we learn how to line two decimals up and say which one is bigger. Let's use money from the corner store!

visual.caption: Zero point two five: 2 tenths and 5 hundredths

steps.say: Here is the big rule. Always compare the tenths first, because tenths are worth more than hundredths. Only if the tenths are exactly the same do you move over and compare the hundredths.

Let's try zero point two five and zero point three. Look at the tenths. Zero point two five has two tenths. Zero point three has three tenths. Three tenths is more than two tenths, so zero point three is the bigger one. Think of dollars: twenty five cents versus thirty cents. Thirty cents buys more.

visual.caption: 25 squares shaded, plus 5 more makes 30 — zero point three is the larger amount

steps.say: Careful! Lots of kids look at zero point two five and say it must be bigger because it has more digits. But more digits does not mean more value. On the number line, zero point three sits to the right of zero point two five, and whatever is further right is always bigger.

visual.caption: The arrow jumps right from 0.25 to 0.3 — right means bigger

steps.say: Now let's order three numbers: zero point four seven, zero point four, and zero point five. Compare tenths first. Four tenths, four tenths, and five tenths. So zero point five is the biggest. The other two both have four tenths, so now check hundredths: seven hundredths beats zero hundredths, so zero point four seven is bigger than zero point four. Smallest to biggest: zero point four, zero point four seven, zero point five.

visual.caption: 0.4, then 0.47, then 0.5 — left to right, smallest to biggest

steps.say: So remember: check the tenths first, and only look at hundredths if the tenths match. A longer decimal is not automatically a bigger decimal.

lesson.answer: Compare tenths first, then hundredths — more digits does not mean a bigger number.

practice.question: At the Granville Island market, a small apple costs zero point six five dollars and a plum costs zero point seven dollars. Draw a number line from zero point six to zero point eight, mark both prices on it, and tell Ms. Yuanyuan which one costs more.
practice.answer: The plum costs more. Zero point seven has seven tenths and zero point six five has only six tenths, so zero point seven is bigger and sits further right on the number line — seventy cents beats sixty five cents.
